laws.rule: The legal age for cannabis in Saskatchewan is 19. Adults may carry up to 30 g of dried cannabis (or equivalent) in public, and buy only from private licensed stores, in person and online.

items.text: The legal age to buy and use cannabis is 19, the same as alcohol. Adults may carry up to 30 g in public. Cannabis is sold through private stores regulated by the Saskatchewan Liquor and Gaming Authority (SLGA).

Using cannabis in public places is banned, and so is using it in a vehicle, as driver or passenger. Set fines include C$200 (about A$203) for using it in a public place or carrying more than 30 g in public, C$300 (about A$305) for possessing or using it in a vehicle, and C$1,000 (about A$1,016) for using it at a school or child care facility, at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = CAD 0.9838.

The legal drinking age is 19. Since 23 May 2023 municipalities and park authorities can pass a bylaw designating outdoor public places, such as parks, where adults may drink; the areas and hours must be posted, and provincial liquor rules still apply there.
